subject: POC environment: ops acceptance milestones & ownership
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha O'Neil <samantha.oneil@gridlytics.com>, Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@gridlytics.com>
Cc: ops+it@gridlytics.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC environment: ops acceptance milestones & ownership

Hi Samantha / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our MAP draft, I wanted to capture the POC environment milestones we discussed and confirm owners and target dates so we can lock the slot for your pilot next month. This email pulls together the minimum dependencies Redwood needs to validate readiness for the POC:

1) Networking: VPC peering or PrivateLink (your preference) + public IP allowlist for our egress endpoints
   - Action: Gridlytics infra to provide preferred connectivity approach, desired CIDR ranges, and expected timeslot for peering
   - Proposed owner: Carlos Ramirez (Gridlytics) / Redwood infra (Vanessa)

2) IP allowlists & NAT egress
   - Action: Confirm static IPs we should expect traffic from, and whether you will route via NAT or use direct peering
   - Deliverable: vpn-ips.csv (placeholder attached)

3) Authentication: SSO / SAML metadata exchange and test user
   - Action: Gridlytics to share IdP metadata + create a test account in the SAML group we can use for the smoke tests
   - Owner: Samantha O'Neil (Gridlytics)

4) Secrets & KMS access
   - Action: Confirm whether Gridlytics will manage secrets (customer-managed KMS) or allow Redwood-managed ephemeral keys for the POC. If customer KMS, please share IAM role or key ARN we can assume for the POC
   - Owner: Gridlytics security team (cc'ed ops+it)

Target close for infra readiness: 2027-05-06 (we'd like one full week of validation before the scheduled POC start on 2027-05-13).

Attachments included: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (MAP with milestones), network-diagram.png (example topology).

Ask: can you confirm owners for each item and provide the SAML metadata + preferred CIDRs by EOD Thursday (2027-04-29)? If that timeline doesn't work, propose the earliest date you can deliver and we'll adjust the MAP accordingly.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0123

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference runtime
From: Samantha O'Neil <samantha.oneil@gridlytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@gridlytics.com>, ops+it@gridlytics.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC environment: ops acceptance milestones & ownership

Thanks Vanessa — good recap. Quick responses inline: 

1) Networking: we prefer VPC peering (simpler for our infra team). Carlos will lead and provide the CIDR ranges. ETA: 2027-04-29 morning.

2) IP allowlists: I'll attach a list of the egress IPs we currently use for external services (vpn-ips.csv). For the Redwood egress, please confirm whether you need TCP/UDP specifics or just source IPs.

3) SAML/SSO: we'll provide SAML metadata and spin up a test user in the 'redwood-poc' group. Security wants to run a quick internal review before distribution — expect final metadata by COB Wednesday (2027-04-28).

4) Secrets/KMS: Gridlytics prefers customer-managed KMS. I'll coordinate with security to produce a role ARN or temporary credentials for the POC. That will likely land on 2027-04-30.

On the timeline, the 2027-05-06 readiness target is tight but doable if we hit the dates above. If anything slips we'll let you know immediately.

Attachments: placeholder vpn-ips.csv (will send final once Carlos confirms network ranges).

Best,
Samantha
Samantha O'Neil
Head of Cloud Ops, Gridlytics
S: +1 617-555-2244
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha O'Neil <samantha.oneil@gridlytics.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@gridlytics.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC environment: ops acceptance milestones & ownership

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Samantha. Two small clarifications from the implementation side: 

- For the IP allowlist: Redwood's runtime will originate from three static egress IPs per region. We only need the source IPs (no special ports beyond 443). I'll attach our canonical list in a follow-up note if helpful.

- For customer-managed KMS: to minimize friction for the POC we can support either (a) granting a short-lived assume-role for Redwood to encrypt/decrypt POC secrets, or (b) you supply encrypted bundles we never decrypt. Option (a) is easier for automated secrets handling. If you go with (a), we can provide a minimal IAM policy to scope access to a single key only.

Markus — can you call out the recommended key lifecycle and any ephemeral key doc links we should share with Gridlytics?

Thanks,
Ben
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha O'Neil <samantha.oneil@gridlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@gridlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC environment: ops acceptance milestones & ownership

Hi all —

Short note from security/implementation perspective:

- Recommended approach for the POC: customer-managed KMS with an assume-role that grants Encrypt/Decrypt on a single key ARN. TTL for the role creds can be set to 1 hour; Redwood requests an audit log stream or read-only role to confirm key usage during validation.

- SAML testing: once we receive metadata, we'll perform a SAML login test using a sandbox account and confirm assertion attributes (email, role). Please include a test username and membership in the 'redwood-poc' group.

Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/platform/kms-ephemeral-keys (implementation checklist)

If Gridlytics can drop SAML metadata (SAML-metadata.xml) and the final vpn-ips.csv into this thread by COB today or early tomorrow, we'll target validation complete by 2027-05-04.

Thanks,
Markus
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
